commander: General der Panzertruppe Hans Freiherr von Funck
notes: Funck's XLVII Panzer Corps committed 2nd Panzer Division (two infantry regiments, two artillery battalions, no tanks) in a counter-attack between Cahagnes and Villers-Bocage 13 June.

commander: General der Panzertruppen Hans Freiherr von Funck
location_qualifier: Caumont-Rauray sector; corps command post not stated
current_activity: XLVII Panzer Corps holding the Caumont-Rauray sector, the fourth and last corps of the line under Panzer Group West
notes: Event date: Breakout and Pursuit ch. 2 p. 30: "On 1 July the corps that faced the Allies lined up from east to west in the following order: LXXXVI, I SS Panzer, II SS Panzer, XLVII Panzer, II Parachute, and LXXXIV"; "The boundary lay just west of Caumont"; ch. 2 p. 29 has the corps forward to the vicinity of Caumont since 13 June. Location: the sector centre; the point is the dataset place Caumont-Rauray sector (midpoint of Caumont-l'Éventé and Rauray), with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the source gives no corps command post place; the sector name comes from the Nafziger order of battle of July 1944, which puts the corps opposite the British XXX Corps in the Caumont-Rauray sector. Relationship: Breakout and Pursuit ch. 2 p. 30: on 28 June Panzer Group West took control of the four corps on the right; the corps is the fourth of the order of 1 July. Commander: General der Panzertruppen Hans Freiherr von Funck (ch. 2 p. 29).

commander: General der Panzertruppen Hans Freiherr von Funck
location_qualifier: attack sector; corps command post not stated
current_activity: XLVII Panzer Corps attack toward Avranches; Funck halts it around noon
notes: Event date: Breakout and Pursuit ch. 24 p. 462-463: the XLVII Panzer Corps commanded the attacking force of three armored divisions (2d SS, 2d and 116th, with the 1st SS to exploit); with tank losses skyrocketing, Funck halted the attack around noon of 7 August and told the troops to dig in. Location: the corps attack sector between Mortain and the Sée; the source gives no corps command post. Location approximate: the point is Mortain, precision 10 km. Commander: General der Panzertruppen Hans Freiherr von Funck (ch. 24 p. 459). Relationship: Hausser, the Seventh Army commander, dealt with Funck directly on the day (p. 462-463); the attack force was constituted under the XLVII Panzer Corps (p. 457).

commander: General der Panzertruppen Hans Freiherr von Funck
current_activity: XLVII Panzer Corps headquarters arrives at Argentan; takes control of 9th Panzer remnants and the 116th
notes: Event date: Breakout and Pursuit ch. 25 p. 502: on 12 August Panzer Group Eberbach assumed command in the Argentan sector; the XLVII Panzer Corps headquarters, having turned over its responsibility at Mortain to the LVIII Panzer Corps, arrived at Argentan and took control of the remnants of the 9th Panzer Division in the Ecouves forest; p. 503: it committed the 116th Panzer Division piecemeal south of Argentan. Location: Argentan, named in the source for the headquarters arrival. Commander: General der Panzertruppen Hans Freiherr von Funck (ch. 25 p. 484).

commander: General der Panzertruppen Hans Freiherr von Funck
location_qualifier: crossing area; corps headquarters not tied to a village
current_activity: XLVII Panzer Corps breakout across the Dives in the St. Lambert-Chambois area
notes: Event date: Breakout and Pursuit ch. 27 p. 548-549: the XLVII Panzer Corps was to open the way for the surrounded forces on the southern flank, crossing the Dives in the St. Lambert-Chambois area; the corps headquarters and the 1st SS Panzer Division had probably fought across the river there early on 20 August and more than likely completed the breakout that afternoon. Location: the St. Lambert-Chambois crossing area; the point is the midpoint of the two places. Location caveat: the Green Book words the corps crossing as probable ("probably", "more than likely"), not certain. Relationship: Hausser issued the order for the XLVII Panzer Corps attack (p. 539) when he commanded the encircled forces.

location_qualifier: destination of the order, not a documented position
current_activity: Blaskowitz orders the XLVII Panzer Corps headquarters from Metz to the Mirecourt-Neufchâteau area
notes: Event date: CMH Lorraine Campaign ch. 4 p. 192-193: "On 4 September he finally reached Luettwitz by phone" and ordered "the XLVII Panzer Corps headquarters down from Metz to take over in the Mirecourt-Neufchâteau area, the base for the proposed operation". Event definition: the order of 4 September; the corps did not necessarily arrive there (p. 193 shows the divisions could not disengage), so the row records the order and the destination. Event support: one source family (CMH). Location: Mirecourt, the first named place of the destination area, with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the destination of the order, not a documented position. Location support: CMH names the area as Mirecourt-Neufchâteau. Commander: General Luettwitz. Context: Lorraine ch. 1 p. 49 has the corps in the First Army line along the Moselle from Arnaville to Bayon on 5 September, so the move was overtaken by events.

current_activity: The XLVII Panzer Corps holds the First Army left wing along the Moselle from Arnaville to Bayon
notes: Event date: CMH Lorraine Campaign ch. 1 p. 49: "The left wing of the First Army was held by the XLVII Panzer Corps, whose sector extended along the Moselle from Arnaville to Bayon, roughly opposite the American XII Corps". Event definition: the situation of 5 September, the date of the First Army front description on p. 47-48. Event support: one source family (CMH). Location: Nancy, the middle of the Arnaville-Bayon sector, with a precision of 25 km. Location approximate: a sector point; no corps headquarters place is given. Location support: CMH names both ends of the sector. Commander: General Luettwitz. Opponents: US XII Corps.

source_locator: R416: p. 234-235; R261: table of 1944, September row
current_activity: The XLVII Panzer Corps falls back to the line Forêt de Parroy-Croismare-Vezouse-Azerailles under the Fifth Panzer Army
notes: Event date: CMH Lorraine Campaign ch. 5 p. 235: "the XLVII Panzer Corps organized to defend a new position which extended from the Forêt de Parroy to Croismare" and "tied in with the Nineteenth Army at the Meurthe River near Azerailles"; Lexikon der Wehrmacht, XLVII Panzerkorps, table 1944: September, 5. Panzerarmee, Heeresgruppe G, "Lothringen". Event definition: the night of 22-23 September; the row is 23 September. Event support: CMH has the day; the Lexikon table is month-level (two families). Location: Lunéville, the middle of the Parroy-Azerailles line, with a precision of 25 km. Location approximate: a sector point; no corps headquarters place is given. Location support: CMH names the line. Commander: General Luettwitz. Opponents: US XV Corps (79th Infantry Division, French 2nd Armored Division).

location_qualifier: reserve position a few miles behind the front; no village is named
current_activity: XLVII Panzer Corps is the army group reserve close behind the Aachen-Roer front
notes: Event date: CMH Siegfried Line Campaign ch. 18 p. 410: "the sector had been accorded the army group reserve, the XLVII Panzer Corps"; ch. 22 p. 518: "the two divisions which made up the OB WEST reserve in this sector, General von Luettwitz' XLVII Panzer Corps". Event definition: the state on 15 November when the Fifth Panzer Army handed over the sector. Event support: one source family (CMH). Location: Setterich with a precision of 10 km, the area behind the front where the corps reserve stood; CMH says only a reserve position a few miles behind the front line. Location approximate: a village point for the reserve area. Location support: CMH puts the reserve behind the XII SS and LXXXI Corps boundary. Commander: General von Luettwitz. Opponents: US Ninth Army.
